newsitem.title: UK: Reuters H1 seen flat on sterling.
newsitem.headline: Reuters H1 seen flat on sterling.

text.p: The strength of the pound is likely to mean flat to marginally lower first-half profit figures from Reuters Holdings Plc, analysts said on Friday.
They forecast pre-tax profit of 330-342 million stg in the six months to June 30, against 342 million in the period last year. The interim dividend is seen at 3.0-3.4 pence per share, up from 2.75p.
Reuters, the global news and information company, will report its first-half figures on Wednesday, July 23.
Chief executive Peter Job said in April the company expected little or no growth in pre-tax profit at the half-year stage if sterling remained strong.
Much of the company's business is denominated in foreign currencies, meaning the pound's rise to its highest levels for six years has a strong impact.
Analysts said attention will focus on underlying revenue growth and in particular the progress of the new 3000 range of financial information products.
They will also seek an update on the company's plans for its cash surplus, which totalled 1.05 billion stg at the end of its last financial year.
